subject: Bridging from current API to Redwood: hosting choice and next milestones
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@avasystems.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@avasystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Bridging from current API to Redwood: hosting choice and next milestones

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the candid product questions. Quick recap + a few qualification items so we can line up the right path (Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private VPC/on-prem):

Summary of call (2 min):
- Primary objective: Replace current LLM API for product search and answer generation without regressing latency or cost.
- Current footprint: ~120 RPS peak across a mix of short chat queries and long-form document scoring.
- Migration sources discussed: existing LLM API (third-party hosted), and a legacy on-prem GPU cluster used for heavy batch scoring.

Open qualification items (please reply inline where possible):
1) Hosting preference: do you have a mandate for Private (VPC or on-prem) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) vs staying on our Hosted API for initial launch?
2) Data residency / compliance: are there regulatory constraints that require on-prem or specific cloud regions?
3) Cutover risk tolerance: do you need a canary/cold-start plan tied to traffic percentage for the first 30 days?
4) Timeline & procurement: target GA date and procurement/contracting windows?
5) Integration constraints: do you expect model weights to be uploaded (self-host) or will you consume via API only?

Attached: MAP-draft.xlsx (mutual action plan, initial owners & milestones). Also linking our short deploy-options brief: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cMAP-draft

Suggested next step: technical deep-dive with your infra lead (30–45m) to capture network/VPC constraints and current token/QPS profiles. Proposed slots: Wed 5/13 10a PT or Thu 5/14 2p PT.

Thanks — I’ll consolidate answers and share a tailored recommendation (hosted-first vs dedicated-on-day-one vs private rollout) and a ballpark cost by next Tuesday.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments: MAP-draft.xlsx (excel, 42KB)
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@avasystems.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@avasystems.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging from current API to Redwood: hosting choice and next milestones

Thanks Neha — good demo. Answers inline below.

Quick answers to qualification items:
1) Hosting preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and to avoid co-tenancy variability. However, we may require a Private VPC option later this year for certain regulated datasets. For launch we prefer Dedicated.
2) Data residency: US-only for now; may need EU controls later.
3) Cutover risk: yes — we prefer a phased canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over two weeks, with automated fallback to current API.
4) Timeline: target internal pilot by 2026-07-01, GA by 2026-09-01. Procurement: our legal/procure timeline is typically 6–8 weeks.
5) Integration: plan is API-only. We do not plan to upload model weights, but we do have custom prompt templates and a small private embedding store.

Notes / constraints:
- Our legacy GPU cluster is used for nightly batch reranks; we may keep it as a fallback for heavy batch scoring but prefer to move real-time inference to Redwood Dedicated.
- SSO/SCIM and VPC peering are must-haves for Dedicated/Private.
- We will need SOC 2 evidence and a security questionnaire answered before procurement gets final sign-off.

Action items we’d like from Redwood:
- Ballpark monthly cost for Dedicated at 100 RPS baseline / 150 RPS burst, and delta to Private VPC pricing.
- Sample canary cutover checklist (networking, KV cache priming, rollback triggers).
- Evidence/SOC2 report and high-level security controls doc.

Jordan
Director of Search Engineering | Ava Systems
jordan.lee@avasystems.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@avasystems.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@avasystems.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridging from current API to Redwood: hosting choice and next milestones

Jordan — thanks for the clear answers. A few clarifying questions so we size the Dedicated config and can provide a reliable ballpark: 
- Typical prompt/token length distribution (p50/p95 tokens) for your real-time requests?
- For batch reranks: what’s the max concurrent batch jobs and average batch size?
- Do you have soft SLA needs (p95 latency target) we should include in the price estimate?

Quick notes on options: 
- Hosted API (fastest path): good for proof-of-concept and short timetables. Limited network isolation, but we can provide private endpoints and encryption-in-flight.
- Dedicated (recommended for your latency predictability): reserved GPU pool with pinning to instance classes, autoscaling for daily bursts, and optional VPC peering for direct egress. Canary rollout capabilities and automatic fallback templates are built into the Console.
- Private VPC / On-prem: we typically recommend this for regulated datasets or EU residency needs. Longer setup (4–8 weeks) and protracted procurement.

What we’ll deliver by next Tue: 1) a Dedicated vs Private pricing delta based on the numbers below, 2) a sample canary cutover checklist, 3) SOC 2 evidence link and security FAQ. Rishi — can you pick up the ball on the canary checklist and SOC2 link?

Proposed deep-dive: Thu 5/14 2p PT works for us; sending a calendar invite.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-deploy-options.pdf (summary, 120KB)

Hi Marissa / Neha — procurement here. A couple of items from our side: 
- We can start procurement paperwork as soon as we have a short SOW and a draft contract (we usually handle NDAs + MSA concurrently). Please include standard security addendum for SOC 2 Type II and encryption-at-rest language.
- We need a procurement lead time estimate and sample SOW with milestones tied to the MAP-draft.xlsx. Our timeline target aligns with Jordan’s GA target; procurement will aim to complete by end of June if we have the legal docs by 5/25.
- Cost approvals: we’ll need a 6–12 month committed pricing option and a monthly consumption fallback.

Also: please include a short section on support SLAs (P1/P2 response windows) and an escalation contact.

Thanks — Samir

procurement@avasystems.com

Appreciate the quick procurement note, Samir — great clarity. Consolidated next steps (owners & dates):
- Marissa: provide draft SOW + MSA template and committed pricing delta (Dedicated vs Private) by Tue 5/19. Deliverable: SOW-draft + price matrix.
- Rishi: SOC 2 Type II report link + security FAQ by Tue 5/19. Deliverable: security-evidence.zip (link).
- Neha: run technical deep-dive (Thu 5/14 at 2p PT) to capture token distributions, canary triggers, and VPC peering requirements; follow-up notes will include a sample canary plan.
- Ava Systems: confirm token p50/p95 and batch job profiles before the deep-dive (Jordan).

I’ll also attach the updated MAP (owners filled in) after the deep-dive. If procurement can provisionally hold 7/01 for pilot start, we’ll align the rollout milestones to that target.

If that all sounds good I’ll drop the calendar invite and a short one-page canary checklist into the Drive.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
